svg.title: Sparse Koopman autoencoder story diagram
svg.desc: Editable method figure for a paper on sparse Koopman autoencoders for multibasin dynamics. Panels show the multibasin problem, sparse Koopman model, support-as-basin-chart idea, and support-routed prediction with periodic re-encoding.

g.inkscape:label: Title block
g.text: Sparse Koopman Autoencoders for Multibasin Dynamical Systems
Sparse latent supports form label-free charts for basin-local linear prediction

g.inkscape:label: Panel A - multibasin problem
g.text: Problem: one global linear map fails on multibasin systems

g.inkscape:label: Panel B - sparse Koopman autoencoder
g.text: Proposed model: sparse latent Koopman autoencoder

g.inkscape:label: Sparse encoder equations
g.text: The coefficients are continuous; the active set is discrete.

g.inkscape:label: Support restricted transition
g.text: Only active latent coordinates participate strongly.
A structure penalty can encourage inactive cross-support entries to stay small.

g.inkscape:label: Panel C - supports as basin indicators
g.text: Core idea: sparse supports become discrete basin indicators

g.inkscape:label: Support families map to basins
g.text: z_S locates the state inside it.

g.inkscape:label: No labels callout
g.text: No basin labels, basin count, or oracle routing are required during training/deployment.

g.inkscape:label: Panel D - support routed prediction and refresh
g.text: Deployment mechanism: support-routed prediction with periodic re-encoding

g.inkscape:label: Trajectory and support refresh story
g.text: Trajectory crosses regions; support is refreshed after each decoded rollout

g.inkscape:label: Stale support vs refreshed support concept
g.text: S(x) selects the relevant active coordinates or local K_S.

g.inkscape:label: Refresh equation strip
g.text: z_k = E(x_k), z_{k+m} = K_S^m z_k, xhat_{k+m}=D(z_{k+m}), refreshed support = S(E(xhat_{k+m}))

g.inkscape:label: Bottom core idea contribution strip
g.text: sparse latent codes expose a discrete support for each state.
Support families act as label-free basin charts; re-encoding lets the chart update during rollout.
